newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Woodside talks price with Western Power.
newsitem.headline: Woodside talks price with Western Power.

text.p: Woodside Petroleum Ltd said on Friday the partners in the North-West Shelf domestic gas venture have agreed with the Western Australian government's Western Power utility to adjourn abribration proceedings and negotiate directly over pricing issues.

The company, which is the operator of the giant North West Shelf gas project, said the domestic venture provides about 116 terajoules per day of natural gas to Western Power under contracts which extend to 2005.

A Woodside spokesman said the original contract was reached in 1984 and contains an option to seek arbitration each time prices are due for renegotiation. He said price details are not revealed due to commercial considerations.

The partners in the North West Shelf domestic venture are Woodside, BHP Petroleum (North West Shelf Pty Ltd), BP Developments Australia Ltd, Chevron Asiatic Ltd, and Shell Development (Australia) Pty Ltd.
